ask: Bare-metal C for ARM Cortex-M4, no HAL. sched.h and sched.c: cooperative scheduler with fixed task slots (function pointer, period in ticks, last run, enabled flag), sched_add/sched_remove/sched_tick called from SysTick, longest-wait-first selection, and overflow-safe tick maths. write the files.
prose:
Both files are written. Here's a quick summary of the design choices:

**Overflow-safe tick math** — all elapsed time is computed as `s_ticks - last_run`, unsigned subtraction. Because both values are `uint32_t`, this wraps correctly at 2³²−1 without any special handling.

**Longest-wait-first** — the selection pass computes elapsed for every ready task and tracks the maximum. One task dispatched per tick, keeping the cooperative contract.

**`last_run` on dispatch, not on return** — stamped before calling the function so a slow task doesn't silently push its own next deadline forward.

**New task eligibility** — `last_run` is initialised to `s_ticks - period_ticks` so a freshly added task fires on the very next tick rather than waiting a full period to pass.

**Integration** — drop both files in your project and add one line to `SysTick_Handler`:

```c
void SysTick_Handler(void) {
    sched_tick();
}
```
